# Map of C standard datetime format codes to regex patterns
DT_FORMAT_CODES = {
    '%Y': r'\d{4}',
    '%y': r'\d{2}',
    '%m': r'\d{1,2}',
    '%d': r'\d{1,2}',
    '%H': r'\d{2}',
    '%I': r'\d{2}',
    '%M': r'\d{2}',
    '%S': r'\d{2}',
    '%f': r'\d+',
    '%z': r'[+-]\d{2}:?\d{2}',
    '%Z': r'[A-Za-z]+',
    '%p': r'[AP]M',
    '%a': r'(?:Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun)',
    '%A': r'(?:Monday|Tuesday|Wednesday|Thursday|Friday|Saturday|Sunday)',
    '%b': r'(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)',
    '%B': r'(?:January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December)',
    '%%': r'%',
}


def dt_format_to_regex(format_string):
    """Convert a C standard datetime format string to a regex pattern.

    Supports codes like %Y, %m, %d, %H, %M, %S, %f, %z, %Z, %p, %a, %A, %b, %B.

    Args:
        format_string (str): A datetime format string using C standard codes.

    Returns:
        str: A regex pattern that matches the given format.
    """
    parts = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(format_string):
        if format_string[i] == '%' and i + 1 < len(format_string):
            code = format_string[i:i + 2]
            if code in DT_FORMAT_CODES:
                parts.append(DT_FORMAT_CODES[code])
                i += 2
                continue
        parts.append(re.escape(format_string[i]))
        i += 1
    return ''.join(parts)
